items.text: SoI has assured Andhra Pradesh that it will take over maintenance costs for the 70 CORS stations after the current contract expires, provide technical upgrades, and ensure the state retains ownership and recognition for its infrastructure. The integration also aligns with the National Geospatial Policy of 2022, which promotes sharing publicly funded data as a “common good.” 2 6. The Andhra Pradesh state invested ₹11.74 crores to establish its CORS network and faces annual maintenance cos ts of ₹50.73 lakhs. The proposed MoU ensures that Andhra Pradesh retains full revenue from private CORS data usage, receives free access for 1,500 state users to the national network, and gets technical support from SoI. A Joint Technical Oversight Committee with equal representation from both sides will monitor decisions, ensuring the state’s interests are protected. 7. The MoU enables the joint operation, maintenance, and integration of the Andhra Pradesh CORS Network into the National CORS infrastructure managed by SoI, while safeguarding the interests and autonomy of the Government of Andhra Pradesh. 8. In view of the above, after careful consideration, Government of Andhra Pradesh hereby decided to enter into memorandum of Understanding with Survey of Ind ia, (SOI), Department of Science and Technology, Government of India, New Delhi, for integrating Andhra Pradesh’s Continuously Operating Reference Station (CORS) network with the National CORS to improve efficiency, avoid duplication, and support national initiatives like Digital India. 9.

The network was established through a contract signed on 7 th October 2019 between the Managing Director, AP Technology Services Limited (on behalf of SSLR, AP), and M/s Hexagon Geo Systems (P) Limited, in consortium with M/s Geovista Technologies (P) Limited. 2. Survey of India (SoI), as the National Mapping Agency, is mandated to create, develop, and maintain the National Geodetic Reference Frame (NGRF) to enable precise and consistent coordinate-based location referencing across the country. 3. SSLR and SoI agree to jointly engage in the operation and maintenance of the Andhra Pradesh CORS Network. SSLR shall continue to operate and maintain the CORS stations during the tenure of the existing contract and any of its amendments, bearing all related expenditures and liabilities during this period. Upon expiry of the said contract and its amendments, SoI shall assume full responsibility for the operation and maintenance of the network for the subsequent five years, including all associated costs and liabilities. To ensure alignment with evolving technical standards, SoI shall upgrade the existing hardware, software, and related infrastructure of the AP CORS Network using its o wn resources. 4. In addition to Clause 3, future enhancements to the CORS receivers—such as support for multi-constellation systems, Indian NavIC, and higher sampling rates—shall be undertaken by SoI. These upgrades shall include: (i) integration of AP COR S Control Centre with the SOI Control Centre (ii) provision of redundant power supply backup at each station, (iii) provision of redundant communication at each station along with installation of essential hardware such as routers, power adapters, chargers, storage, and security devices, and (iv) deployment of appliances for surge and lightning protection. All associated expenditures shall be borne by SoI. 5. Operation and Maintenance (O&M) services shall be oversaw jointly monitored by SoI and SSLR. The SLA for O&M shall be as per SoI national contractual agreement. 6. During the O&M period under SoI, SSLR shall permit access to CORS station monuments for SoI personnel and authorized representatives solely for the maintenance of installed equipment and appliances, and shall provide the necessary AC power supply at these sites. 7. Ownership of the existing CORS base stations, including all software, hardware, and appliances installed by SSLR, shall remain with SSLR. Ownership of any additional hardware installed for upgradation shall rest with SoI. Any alteration, upgradation, replacement, or removal of existing or new hardware shall be undertaken only with mutual agreement and prior written intimation to SSLR. Any hardware integration or asset augmentation shall be formally documented through a jointly issued handover note and asset approval certificate specifying ownership, configuration, and inventory status.

Changes to technical policies—including firmware or software updates, system architecture modifications, or protocol revisions—shall be made only after consultation with SSLR and documented by the 8 Joint Te chnical Committee to ensure traceability, accountability, and operational continuity. 8. Raw GNSS data from CORS stations installed by SSLR in Andhra Pradesh shall be shared with SoI in real time. Any expenditure incurred for additional software, hardware, internet connectivity, or power backup required for data sharing shall be borne by SoI. 9. The shared raw GNSS data may be used by SoI for both commercial and non-commercial purposes, including the maintenance of the National Geodetic Reference Frame, geod etic network harmonization, disaster management planning, support for Government-to- Government (G2G) initiatives, location -based services for government and private users, and promoting research and development in geodesy, geospatial technologies, and alli ed sectors such as logistics, construction, agriculture, inland and maritime navigation, and Earth system observations. Any commercial use of the shared data, apart from the standard position augmentation service for surveying and mapping activities, shall be intimated in advance in writing to the Commissioner and Director, SSLR, Government of Andhra Pradesh. 10.

Recognizing that the initial capital investment in establishing the existing CORS network was made by AP Survey, Settlement & Land Records (AP SSL R), SoI has agreed that all revenue collected (as per pricing policy of AP SSLR) from private users accessing CORS data and services in Andhra Pradesh will be collected by AP SSLR directly. This will be operationalised through a direct linkage of APSSLR's designated bank account to SoI CORS portal. SoI will not require any revenue sharing from the existing setup, for the development of this sector. The GoAP retains full rights to distribute CORS data via its official channels and shall manage user access, billing, and service delivery independently, without interference or duplication by SoI. 11. SoI may share raw GNSS data and derivative products from the Andhra Pradesh CORS Network internationally, strictly under Government of India treaty commitments rela ted to global geodetic reference frames, early warning systems, and Earth observation. Such sharing shall be carried out with prior intimation to the Commissioner and Director, SSLR, Government of Andhra Pradesh. The shared data must be clearly attributed a s "AP CORS – Government of Andhra Pradesh" and shall not be combined with other data sets in a way that obscures state ownership. 12. SoI shall register GoAP users on its control centre for at least a minimum of 1,500 concurrent users, for accessing CORS network products and services at free of cost.

SoI shall share raw GNSS data collected from its own continuously operating reference stations in areas neighbouring Andhra Pradesh, along with derivative products and rea l- time services, to facilitate surveying, mapping, and GIS -related work by SSLR within Andhra Pradesh and in inter-state border regions. This sharing shall be done in accordance with the "Guidelines for Acquiring and Producing Geospatial Data and Geospatia l Data Services Including Maps" issued by the Department of Science and Technology, Government of India, without any charges. 18. A Joint Technical Oversight Committee (JTOC), with equal representation from SoI and the Government of Andhra Pradesh (including technical members nominated by SSLR), shall be constituted as the primary governance body to oversee all operational, technical, and data-sharing matters related to the APCORS Network. The Committee shall review and approve policies, upgrades, and services; resolve grievances; and ensure alignment with both governments data policies and strategic and sovereign data interests. The JTOC shall meet on a half -yearly basis, or as needed, maintaining signed minutes for transparency and accountability. Survey of India (SoI), Ministry of Science and Technology, GoI.

In the reference 5th read above, the Inspector General, Registration & Stamps has submitted the financial implications stating that the provisional total financial implications is approximately Rs.16.25 Crores and both TUDA and enjoyers are benefiting from the said scheme. He has opined that the registration charges on conveyance deeds may be paid either by TUDA or the enjoyers. He has requested the Government to take further action in the matter. 3. Government after careful examination of the matter, have decided to exempt the Stamp Duty under Section 9 (a) of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 and Registration Fee under Section 78 of the Andhra Pradesh Registration Act, 1908, in respect of all conveyance deeds executed by Tirupati Urban Development Authority (TUDA), to an extent of total land Ac.286.83(123.09+163.74), in favour of beneficiaries/allottees of the Settipalli Land Pooling Scheme, Tirupati District. 4. Accordingly, the following notification will be published in an Extraordinary Issue of the Andhra Pradesh Gazette, dated:12.01.2026. P.T.O. NOTIFICATION-I In exercise of the powers conferred by clause (a) of Sub section (1) of Section 9 of the Indian Stamp Act 1899, the Governor of Andhra Pradesh hereby exempt the Stamp Duty for execution of all conveyance deeds executed by Tirupati Urban Development Authority (TUDA), to an extent of total land Ac.286.83(123.09+163.74), in favour of beneficiaries/allottees of the Settipalli Land Pooling Scheme, Tirupati District.

As reported by the Collector, Chittoor subjected lands are in continuous possession and cultivation by the local farmers from more than 50 years and most of these farmers are small and marginal farmers depended upon these lands for their livelihood. d. items.text: Virtual meeting of the drought committee has been held on 28.03.2025. The Committee have examined the proposals in detail received from the District Collectors for declaration of Drought affected Mandals in Rabi 2024-25 with reference to the guidelines prescribed by Government of India Manual for Drought Management-2016 and also recommended to the Government that (51) Mandals as Drought affected (37 mandals as Severe Drought and 14 Mandals as Moderate Drought) in Six (6) Districts i.e., Kurnool, Nandyal, Ananthapuramu, Sri Satya Sai, YSR and Prakasam. 2. Government, after careful examination of the reports furnished by the District Collectors in the reference 3 rd read above and recommendations of the Committee on Drought in the reference 4 th read above, decided to issue a Notification (Annexure-I) for declaration of (51) Mandals (as in the Annexure-II) as Drought affected (37 Mandals as Severe Drought and 14 Mandals as Moderate Drought) in Six (6) Districts i.e., Kurnool (9 severe and 1 moderate), Nandyal (1 severe and 4 moderate), Ananthapuramu (6 severe and 1 moderate), Sri Satya Sai (1 severe and 1 moderate), Prakasam (11 severe and 6 moderate) and YSR (9 severe and 1 moderate). 3. The District Collectors concerned shall issue the notification in the District Gazette as mentioned in Annexure-I & II in Telugu and take immediate further necessary action. (PTO) :: 2 :: 4.

items.text: 1st read above. Virtual meeting of the drought committee has been held on 29.10.2025. The District Collectors concerned shall issue the notification in the District Gazette as mentioned in Annexure -I & II in Telugu and take immediate further necessary action. (PTO) :: 2 :: 4. From the APSDMA, e-file computer No. 3114045. &&& ORDER: As per the provisions of the 15th Finance Commission and instructions of the Ministry of Home Affairs, funds under the Recovery & Reconstruction Funding Window (30%) of SDRF/NDRF may be utilised for long-term recovery and reconstruction measures, in accordance with the Disaster Management Act, 2005, based on Post-Disaster Needs Assessment (PDNA). 2. In the G.O. 3 rd read above, Government have adopted the Guidelines on Constitution and Administration of Recovery and Reconstruction Funding Window under National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) / State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) for implementation in the State. 3. In the G.O. 4 th read above, Government have constituted an appraisal committee for appraisal/evaluation of the proposals/projects under Recovery and Reconstruction Funding Window of SDRF/NDRF. 4. As per the GOI guidelines, the State Disaster Management Authority (SDMA) shall act as the nodal entity for planning and implementation of recovery and reconstruction measures, and the State Government is required to conduct PDNA in the aftermath of severe disasters by constituting a Multi-Sectoral Team. Hence, it is decided to constitute a Multi-Sectoral Team for the preparation of Post Disaster Needs Assessment (PDNA) reports/projects/proposals in disaster-affected districts/sectors for utilization of SDRF/NDRF funds, as per the guidelines. items.text: 5. Minutes of the Meeting of the Committee on Drought held on 30.09.2026. ***** O R D E R : Declaration of Kharif Drought should be done by 31 st October as per the Drought Manual . Due to 53.4% rainfall deficit recorded during the months of June–August, 2026, and the prevailing El Niño conditions , by taking into consideration of the relevant drought indicators based on data available for the period from June to August, 2026 , it is proposed to undertake early declaration of drought for Kharif-2026. 2. Rain fall data from 01.06.2026 and Dry Spell data from 07.06.2026 (Monsoon entered date 06.06.2026 issued by IMD) upto 31.08.2026 have been taken into consideration for assessing the Mandatory Indicators. An average rainfall of 197.6 mm has been received against the normal rainfall of 424.3 mm from 01-06-2026 to 31-08-2026. 3. Basically 3 steps are involved in finding out the drought severity of each Mandal. Step-1 : Mandatory data application (Rain fall deviation, Dry spell). Step-2 : Impact indicators data application [ Sown area index, Remote Sensing Index (Vegetation Condition Index), Moisture Adequacy Index, Hydrology Index (Reservoir Storage Index and Ground Water Index) ] (P.T.O) :: 2 :: Step-3 : Ground Truthing. In the references 3 rd read above , all the District Collectors have been requested to submit D rought proposals including NIL reports in respect of all the remaining urban and rural Mandal’s (excluding the 388 Mandals which were already declared as drought affected in the early Kharif Season-2026) in the prescribed proformas, as per the Drought Manual by taking into consideration of the data pertaining to Mandatory Indicators and Impact indicators and Ground T ruthing report for the period from 01 -06-2026 to 30 -09-2026 for declaration of Dro ught for Kharif Season, 2026. 3. In the references 4 th read above, Drought proposals have been received from all the District Collectors for the Kharif Season– 2026, covering the period from 01.06.2026 to 30.09.2026, along with all the prescribed formats and supporting documents, including Trigger -I, Trigger-II and set -off mandal details, Statement -4, Form-11 and Ground Truthing Reports, in accordance with the Drought Manual. Out of the 28 districts in Andhra Pradesh, three districts, namely Palnadu (28 mandals), Prakasam (28 mandals) and Annamayya (25 mandals), have already been covered under the Early Kharif Season–2026 drought declaration, with all mandals in these districts having been declared drought-affected. Accordingly, the final drought assessment for the Kharif Season – 2026 is being considered for the remaining 25 Districts. Of these 25 districts, 17 districts have been proposed to be treated as non -drought districts, while the remaining 8 districts, namely 1.Kakinada 2.Eluru 3.Krishna 4.Markapuram 5.Kurnool 6.Ananthapuram 7.Sri Sathya Sai 8.YSR Kadapa, have proposed a total of 24 mandals for declaration as drought -affected under th e final drought assessment for the Kharif –2026 Season. 5. A Virtual meeting of the Drought Committee constituted vide G.O.6th read above, to scrutinize the proposals submitted by the District Collectors for declaration of Drought Affected Mandals was held on 28.10.2026. 6. The Drought Committee have scrutinized the proposals in detail with reference to the guidelines prescribed in the Manual for Drought Management, 2016 issued by the Government of India, and recommended 24 mandals (12 Mandals as Severe Drought affected and 12 Mandals as Moderate Drought affected ) for declaration as Drought affected during Kharif Season – 2026 in Eight (8) districts, Viz.

Proposal received from Commissioner PR&RD, Date: 28-01-2026. -(o0o)- ORDER: The 73 rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992 mandates that State Governments ensure Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) function as institutions of self- government. Gram Panchayats are the basic Units of Village Governance, promoting locally responsible Administration and decentralisation. The Government of Andhra Pradesh, while recognising and considering diversity and varying characteristics of the rural population and settlements and Geographical features both in plain and Tribal Rural Areas, have decided to initiate policy reforms in Gram Panchayat Administration to suit the present-day developments in Administration which aims to realign resources to Country Planning, Service Delivery and Community Development. 2. In the State of Andhra Pradesh, the Gram Panchayat Administration evolves through the formation of Notified and Non -Notified Gram Panchayats, and the introduction of the Cluster System based on the income of the Gram Panchayat. 3. In the G.O. 1st read above, the Government introduced the Village Secretariat System, sanctioning the posts of Panchayat Secretaries Grade-V and Grade-VI. In view of these significant reforms in grassroots-level administration, it has become necessary to reassess the existing cluster system and undertake a re-categorisation of the Gram Panchayats to ensure effective implementation and administrative efficiency. 4. In the G.O.

items.text: In view of these significant reforms in grassroots-level administration, it has become necessary to reassess the existing cluster system and undertake a re-categorisation of the Gram Panchayats to ensure effective implementation and administrative efficiency. 4. In the G.O. 2nd read above, and in order to address the current needs and requirements of Gram Panchayat administration, the Government has constituted a committee to undertake a comprehensive review of the re -categorisation of Gram Panchayats and to recommend an appropriate staffing pattern. // 2 // 5. In the reference 3rd read above, the Committee had submitted a Comprehensive report along with recommendations for the re-categorisation of the Gram Panchayats and an indicative Staffing Pattern. The Committee have recommended the following criteria for recategorization of Gram Panchayats into three (3) categorie s and the Rurban Gram Panchayat category. Proposed Grade Plain Area Scheduled Area Rurban Gram Panchayat (1) Population above 10,000 (or) (2) Income above Rs 1 crore Population above 5,000 Grade-I Gram Panchayat (1) Population above 3,000 and below 10,000 (or) (2) Income above Rs. 30 Lakhs and below Rs. 1 Crore (or) (3) Mandal Headquarter Gram Panchayat (1) Population above 2500 and below 5000 (or) (2) Mandal Headquarter Gram Panchayat Grade-II Gram Panchayat Population above 2,000 and below 3,000 Population above 1,500 and below 2,500 Grade-III Gram Panchayat Population below 2000 Population below 1500 6. items.text: In the G.O. 5th read above, orders were issued for the restructuring of the Panchayat Raj Department based on the recommendations of the Committee and the detailed proposals submitted by the Commissioner, PR&RD. Among the various aspects covered under the overall framework and terms of restructuring, one of the key issues pertains to the re-categorization of Gram Panchayats. 7. In the reference 7th read above, after consulting the District Collectors of the State, the Commissioner, PR&RD submitted proposals to the Government for district- wise re-categorization of the existing Gram Panchayats into three (3) categories, namely: Grade-I, Grade-II, Grade-III, and Rurban Gram Panchayats, in accordance with the guidelines issued in the G.O. 5th read above. 8. The Government, after careful examination of the proposal submitted by the Commissioner, PR&RD, hereby issues orders re-categorising the Gram Panchayats in Sri Potti Sriramulu Nellore District, which was notified vide G.O. 6th read above. Accordingly, the Collector has requested the Government to accord permission for conversion of the said extent from Grazing Ground Poramboke to Assessed Waste Dry (AWD) under the relevant provisions, to facilitate establishment of the proposed Industrial Park. 2. In the 2 nd reference cited above, the Revenue Divisional Officer, Kuppam, Chittoor District addressed to the Collector, Chittoor District has reported that, as per the Village Accounts, a total extent of Ac.464.84 cents of Government Poramboke land is available within the jurisdiction of Pogurupalle Gram Panchayat, comprising Anganamalakothuru, Lingapuramdinne, and Pogurupalle Revenue Villages. Further, it has been reported that an extent of Ac.24.36 cents of Gutta Poramboke land has been identified and proposed to be earmarked for grazing purposes as compensatory land in lieu of the proposed diversion of Ac.28.59 cents of Grazing Ground Poramboke land.

The Director Electrical Safety and Chief Electrical Inspector to Government has submitted a proposal to the Government in the reference lst read above and requested the Government to issue notification to mandate internal and external electricity installation works to be carried out by Licensed Professional and mandate qualification of Third Party carrying out electrical wiring installation works. 4. Accordingly, the Government after careful examination of the matter, hereby issues the following notification: i. The internal and external electricity installation works shall be carried out by Licensed Professional I Company in the premises of or on behalf of any Consumer, Supplier, Owner or Occupier for the purpose of supply of electricity. The Licensed Professional I Company shall obtain License for Electrical contractors under "The Andhra Pradesh Electrical Licensing Rules, 2025' and shall employ at least One (1) Supervisor holding a Certificate of Page I of 2 competency and permit and TWo (2) wiremen holding a certificate of Competency and Permits issued under the said Rules. The Licensed Contractor shall inspect the internal / external electrical installation at least once in year' The License Professional Company shall issue "Certificate of Compliance" for every inspection conducted for internal and external installation. The quality check or final inspection of the internal and external electricity installation work is mandated to be inspected by a Third Party. The quality check for internal and external installation shall be performed at least once in a Year. Further, the education qualification and experience for Third Party carrying out electrical wiring installation work shall be: For Su a.

These rules extend to the whole State of Andhra Pradesh. 3. These rules shall come into force on the date of publication in the Official Gazette. 2. Accordingly, the proposal of M/s. Clean Renewable Energy Hybrid Six Private Limited received from the Vice Chairman & Managing Director, New & Renewable Energy Development Corporation of Andhra Pradesh (NREDCAP) was placed before State Investment Promotion Board (SIPB) meeting held on 18-09-2026 with recommendations of the State Investment Promotion Committee in its meeting held on 07-09-2026. 6. Accordingly, the SIPB after detailed discussion, has agreed the following: i. for allocation of 118.80 MW AC/ 155.20 MWp DC Solar Power Project in Kasanur and Balapanur villages of Simhadripuram Mandal & Telluru and Madur villages of Thondur mandal in YSR Kadapa District under AP Integrated Clean Energy Policy 2024 without overlapping with the areas already allotted to other developers for RE power capacities.

The Water can be spared based on the subject to the availability of water in the Thunduru Branch Channel. 2. The water drawn from the Source should be utilized for the purpose for which permission is granted. 3. The industry shall pay one year water charges as advance and any amount due to the department before entering into agreement. 4. Under any circumstances, the consumptive utilization should not exceed the quantum of water allotted by the department. 5. Digital Water meters and measuring devices should be installed at the pump house by the industry at their own cost to measure the water consumed and should be made available to the Department authorities and the representatives of the users shall be present at all times for inspection. The water meter shall be periodically calibrated and kept sealed. The period of calibration will be specified by the department. 6. The firm should pay security deposit at 5% on water charges for which permission is granted. 7.

In the minutes of meeting it was stated that the ENC (PR) has informed that Builders’ Association of India, AP had represented that due to COVID-19 pandemic and its restrictions, works under Roads could not be completed within prescribed period and consequently, the experience / qualification of most of the contractors have lapsed and they would become ineligible for tendering for not processing the required qualifications during the 5 years block period and hence requested to consider 10 years block period instead of 5 years block period for qualification and bid capacity for all road works being taken up in both R&B and PR Depts. 4. In the reference 4 th read above, the Commissioner, Commissionerate of tenders, Vijayawada submitted that during Covid Pandemic Period due to restriction in mobilization of men and machinery, less number of works were taken up and some works have been stalled, due to migration of labour. 5. items.text: RULES 1. Introduction: (1) In keeping with the will of the Government to build ‘People’s Capital’ and for building the necessary concomitant infrastructural projects like airports, ports and all other necessary projects, the procurement mechanism of the land has been designed to be a voluntary scheme. It is based on mutual consensus between the land owners and the State/Authority. This is a unique method of procurement of land which is named and styled as ‘Land Pooling Scheme. This Scheme has been designed for developing the Capital Region wherein the land parcels owned by individual farmers and owners or group of owners are consolidated by the Authority under a development scheme. (2) The Land Pooling Scheme itself is a better scheme formulated by the Andhra Pradesh State Legislature owing to the mandate enabled under Sections 107 & 108 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013. By virtue of the surrender made by the land owners participating in the Land Pooling Scheme, the title in the offered land stands transferred in favour of the State/Authority by virtue of the acceptance given by the Competent Authority representing the State/Authority under Section 48(1) of the AP CRDA Act, 2014. According to the agreed Developmental Scheme under Section 43(4)(a) of the AP CRDA Act, 2014, the reconstituted plot is allotted in favour of the land owner who participated in the Land Pooling Scheme in the same area or in any other vicinity land in a single separate sector or in a group of sectors. (3) These rules are applicable to the Capital Region.

The broad objective of the scheme is to do justice to the families affected by the construction of a Livable and Sustainable Capital Region for the State of Andhra Pradesh and also to the farmers and land owners in the Capital Region and also to make them avail a better compensation and also with a view to make them Partners in the State Development Process. This unique Land Pooling Scheme is designed in such a manner that the participant land owners are fairly and betterly compensated with the allotment of the reconstituted plot along with the developed infrastructure. 2. Short title: These Rules may be called as ‘Andhra Pradesh Capital Region Land Pooling Scheme (Formulation and Implementation) Rules 2025’. 3. Applicability: These rules shall be applicable to the entire area notified as ‘Capital Region’ under Section 3(1) of the Act except the Capital City Area which shall be continued to be governed by the Andhra Pradesh Capital City Land Pooling Scheme (Formulation and Implementation) Rules, 2015. 5. Process and Method to be followed by the Government/ Authority for implementing the Land Pooling Scheme: (1) The Government/Authority shall accept the request from any village or group of villages or group of landowners/farmers expressing their consent to participate in the Land Pooling Scheme. The said request would be considered as a voluntary participation of the landowners/farmers in the Land Pooling Scheme under Section 55(2) of the Act. (2) The Commissioner is the Competent Authority, can identify the lands so offered for Land Pooling Scheme. (3) After such identification made by the Commissioner, he shall obtain the approval of the Authority for initiating the Land Pooling Scheme in the identified area under Section 55(3) of the Act. (4) If the Government itself identifies and notifies the intention for any area for Land Pooling Scheme under Section 43(5) & (6) of the Act, the approval of the Authority is not required. (5) Once the Commissioner identifies and gets the approval of the Authority to proceed with the Land Pooling Scheme, the Commissioner/Competent Authority is entitled to declare its intention under Section 55(4) of the Act and invite objections under Section 55(5) in the prescribed format in Notification I .

In this regard, the Competent Authority is entitled to direct the concerned Revenue officials or the units/teams/officials formed by the Competent Authority/Authority/Government to verify and report back within 7 days about the claim of the consenting land owners under Section 3(6) of the Act. Such form and manner may include authentication with a One Time Password or facial recognition or biometric method. (c) The extent of the land so surrendered is physically cross verified through the Surveyor or the units/teams/officials formed by the Competent Authority to ensure the physical availability of the extent offered for surrender. Authority’s Rights (1) The land use of the land affected by Land Pooling Scheme shall automatically stand changed to the land use proposed under the approved Masterplans/Developmental Plans/Zonal Plans/Area Developmental Plans. But, the Land Pooling Ownership Certificate Holder’s reconstituted plot shall always be allocated in residential and commercial areas only. (2) The Authority wherever it deems necessary by duly recording reasons thereof, has the right to merge, split, alter, or revise one or more or all the components of the land pooling scheme and implement the developmental scheme accordingly. (3) The Authority in the overall interest of the development of the area and for the reasons specifically mentioned may take up the realignment of road network which are proposed/notified in the sanctioned masterplans/developmental plans can be realigned to suite the developmental scheme. (4) The Authority is obligated to reserve/earmark the land for the public purposes mentioned under the Developmental Schemes and Land Pooling Schemes as per Section 44 read with Section 53 of the Act.

items.text: (4) The Authority is obligated to reserve/earmark the land for the public purposes mentioned under the Developmental Schemes and Land Pooling Schemes as per Section 44 read with Section 53 of the Act. (5) The Authority is entitled to undertake the whole or part of the Development Process under the Land Pooling Scheme by itself or it may get the works done through any contractor/consultant/Local Body or the Urban Body. (6) The Authority may develop the land under Land Pooling Scheme either by itself or by entering any partnership with any reputed executing company/agency having relevant experience in the field of development of lands, by inviting bids through tenders. (7) The Authority will not enter any land title disputes, if any title over any land falling within the Final Land Pooling Scheme is in dispute, the Authority will keep the disputed claim under abeyance while proceeding with developmental activity in Land Pooling Scheme. (8) Once the civil court’s judgement attains finality the same would be implemented by the Authority by issuing the LPOC to the Judgement and Decree holder. 18. Authority’s Obligations under the Land Pooling Scheme: (1) The Authority is obligated to complete the development of the land taken under Land Pooling Scheme and simultaneously allocate the reconstituted plot in favour of the participating landowner/farmer as per the agreed terms under the Development Agreement. (2) The Authority shall duly acknowledge surrender of the land under Form-IV. (3) The Authority shall allot reconstituted plot by drawing of lots to avoid hostile and one-sided allocation and with a view to avoid any partisan attitude. This allocation shall always be in a fair and transparent manner.

This allocation shall always be in a fair and transparent manner. (4) If any plots are hit by any roads, (veedi sula plots) such plots shall not be included in the lottery process and shall not be allotted in favour of the landowners. (5) The Authority shall reallot the reconstituted plot in a single separate sector or in a group of sectors in the same vicinity or any other revenue village, area. Such reallocation can be made for a group of owners in one lot or in a group of plots at one place as per their joint request, enabling them to combinedly develop the common allocation as per their request. Such group of persons sometimes may be from one single family or may be friends or like-minded persons. (6) The LPOC in favour of the landowners is the proof of title, ownership and possession in favour of the landowner/plot, such Certificates shall be handed over to the landowners within 9 months of the surrender of the land. (7) The Authority shall handover the actual physical possession of reconstituted plot within 12 months of the date of notification of final Land Pooling Scheme. (8) The Authority shall complete the development of the LPS area as per the Notified Development Scheme within all the promised amenities and infrastructure within 3 years from the date of issue of LPOC.

(9) The Authority shall prepare the developmental scheme to be developed in the Land Pooling Scheme lands and obtain the requisite layouts and statutory permissions at their own cost and are obligated to develop the physical infrastructure according to the Statutory Rules and Regulations. (10) The Government/Authority is obligated to develop sector roads/internal roads/ infrastructure/services including water supply lines, power supply, rainwater harvesting, sewage treatment facilities, water treatment facilities, etc., in the land allocated to the landowners as reconstituted plots. (11) The Authority shall develop infrastructure facilities, roads, parks, cremation facility for all religions, community needs etc. and incorporate them into the development scheme at appropriate places. (12) The Authority is obligated to allocate the land for construction of houses to the blue collared employees/houseless & landless poor persons who live in the respective villages and the employees who migrate into the capital area for the purpose of working in all Governmental organizations. (13) The Authority is obligated to develop the Final Land Pooling Scheme land in a time bound manner by duly following all the master plan road patterns, by providing the physical infrastructure as per Section 46 of the Act, and by also providing traffic and transportation infrastructure which will include the road, metro and railway corridors.

Procedural Compliances to be followed by the Competent Authority: (1) Declaration of Intention under Section 55 of the Act for taking up the Land Pooling Scheme shall be notified by the Commissioner/Competent Authority by earmarking the area to be taken up for Land Pooling Scheme. This shall be the First Notification and it is issued in the prescribed format under Notification-I. (2) The Notification shall invite objections and suggestions and invite Surrender Forms from the Landowners who are interested to participate and surrender the land in the Land Pooling Scheme. Under Section 55(4) of the Act, 30 days time from the date of publication of the Notification is to be given to all the landowners/farmers for responding to the said Notification . (3) The Competent Authority shall conduct an hearing as per Section 55(5) of the Act during the above prescribed 30 days time and consider such objections and suggestions. The Competent Authority may agree with the suggested modifications and suggestions and implement them or disapprove them. If the Competent Authority decides to implement the objections/suggestions the same shall be notified in the prescribed format under Notification-IA.

(4) There after the Competent Authority shall issue Draft Notification of the Land Pooling Scheme in the prescribed format in Notification-II consultation with the landowners under Section 56(1) of the Act, with regards to the provisions to be made in the Development Scheme as per Section 44 of the Act, A period of thirty (30) days from date of publication of this notification shall be provided to the land owners to submit their responses. All such consultation shall be recorded in writing in the relevant Land pooling scheme. (5) The Final Notification of the Land Pooling Scheme under Section 57 of the Act shall be published by the Authority after considering the objections and suggestions if any within 180 days from the declaration of intent. This shall be the Third Notification of the Land Pooling Scheme, published in the prescribed format under Notification-III. (6) The Competent Authority shall also execute a Deed of Contract in favour of the landowner, whereunder the Authority/Developer will undertake to develop the said land as per the promised agreed Contractual terms and this Contract is in the prescribed format as Form-V. This Contract will be deemed to be a Statutory Contract which will be enforceable under the public law remedy. (7) Once the Final Notification is published, the landowners shall be given Plot Wise Land Pooling Ownership Certificate (“LPOC”) in the prescribed format appended to these Rules as Form-VI as per Section 57(3) & (4).

(3) The Authority/Commissioner may extend time limits for any of the activities mentioned under these rules in respect of any village for valid reasons. The land is adjacent to Anakapalli - Sabbavaram Road and it is very close to Anakapalli town. As per the report of the Engineering Wing, already an amount of Rs.170.34 Lakhs was incurred towards the registration charges and also development of the layout. The land is plain and very much suitable for housing activity and there is immense need and demand for housing in Anakapalli Town and the project will be financially viable for VMRDA. 3. He has further submitted that, as per section 29 of the 2 APMRUDA Act – 2016, the Competent Authority for land pooling scheme shall be appointed by the Government only. The MC, VMRDA has, therefore, requested that necessary orders may be issued on continuation of the process of land pooling to finality since it is pending for more than 18 years and if so, the Revenue Divisional Officer, Anakapalli may be appointed as the Competent Authority to take up this land pooling scheme. 4.

Pursuant to the proposals received under Section 55(2) of the APCRDA Act, 2014, in the reference 4 th read above the Commissioner, APCRDA has submitted th e “Mangalagiri Gold Cluster Land Pooling Scheme (Formu lation & Implementation) Rules, 2025, for implementation of the “Mangalagiri Gold Cluster Land Pooling Scheme” over an extent of 78.01 acres in Atmakur Village of Mangalagi ri Mandal, Guntur District, for the establishment of a Gems and Jewellery Park within the Capital Region, under sub1section (3) of Section 55 of the APCRDA Act. 3. Whereas, the Government have decided to develop a Gold Cluster exploring the potential benefits of an Integrated Manufacturing a nd Retail Zone in Mangalagiri Assembly Constituency consisting of a Gems and Jewel lery Park which includes a luxurious Mega Mall for Gold and Diamond Jewellery, Manufacturing Hub, Skill Development Centre and a Residential & Community Fa cilities in the proposed Gold Cluster with a aim at to achieve rapid growth of $ 100 Bn Indian Jewellery Market.

And whereas, the land pr ocurement mechanism has been designed to be voluntary and based on c onsensual pr ocess of land p ooling. L and p ooling mechanism is mainly adopted f or d evelopment of an integrated Gold Cluster in Mangalagiri Assembly Constituency wherein the land parcels owned by individuals or group of owners are leg all y consoli dated by transfer of ownership right s to th e Auth ority, which later transfers th e ownership of a part of the land back to th e land owners for undertaking of development for such areas. According to the agreed Developmental Scheme under Section 43(4) of t he APCRDA Act, 2014, the reconstituted plot is allotted in favour of the land owner who participated in Land Pooling Scheme in the same area. 5. And whereas, these rules are applicable to the notified area in Atmak ur Village of Mangalagiri Mandal where a special devel opment scheme under “Mangalagiri Gold Cluster Land Pooling Scheme “ is taken up for establishment of Gems and Jewellery Park in the notified area. T he broad objective of the scheme is to do justice to the families affected by the development of Gold Cluster by making the land owners as partners in development. 6. Now, therefore, the Government have decided to mak e the Mangalagiri Gold Cluster Land Pooling Scheme (Formulation & Implementation) Rules, 2025. 7.

The PS to Principal Secretary to Government, MA&UD Dept., Sf/Sc //FORWARDED :: BY ORDER// SECTION OFFICER NOTIFICATION In exercise of the powers conferred by sub1section (1) read with clause (f) of sub1 section (2) of Section 18 of Andhra Pradesh Capital Region Development Authority Act, 2014 [Act 11 of 2014] , the Government of Andhra Pra desh hereby make the following rules, namely, the Mangalagiri Gold Cluster Land Po oling Scheme (Formulation & Implementation) Rules, 2025. RULES 1. Short title and Extent: (1) These rules may be called as The Mangalagiri Gold Cluster Land Pooling Scheme ( Formulation & Implementation ) Rules, 2025. (2) They shall extend to the lands required to mak e special development scheme for development of Mangalagiri Gold Cluster area i n connection with., establish a Gems and Jewellery Park etc., to cater to the needs of the State of Andhra Pradesh. (3) They shall come into force with effect from the date of publication in the Andhra Pradesh Gazette.

'Act' means the Andhra Pradesh Capital Region Dev elopment Authority Act, 2014. b. “Authority” means constituted under Sub1section (1 ) of Section 4 of the APCRDA Act, 2014. c. “Appellate Authority” means the District Collect or, Guntur and includes the Joint Collector, Guntur. d. “Assigned land” means lands assigned by the Gover nment to the landless poor persons under the rules for the time being in force, subject to the condition of non1alienation and includes lands allotted or trans ferred to landless poor persons under the relevant law for the time being in force relating to land ceiling and the word “assigned” shall construed accordingly. e. “Competent Authority” means Revenue Divisional Off icer/Sub1Collector, Tenali and includes any other officer not below the rank of Deputy Collector appointed by the Government of Andhra Pradesh. f. “Government” means the Government of Andhra Prad esh. g. “Mangalagiri Gold Cluster” means Development of a Gems and Jewellery Park which includes a luxurious Mega Mall for Gold and Diamond Jewellery, Manufacturing Hub, Skill Development Centre and a Res idential & Community Facilities in the proposed Gold Cluster for its development. h. “Original assignee” means a person to whom land is assigned under assignment rules or under Andhra Pradesh Board of R evenue executive instructions and includes his heirs or successors in interest. i.

(2) Pursuant to the notification issued under sub1s ection (4) of Section 55 of the Act, the Competent Authority shall issue a notice in Form -1. (i) Inviting objections and suggestions on the proposed Land Pooling Scheme (LPS) in Form 2 from the land owners within fifteen days from the da te of publication; (ii) inviting participation of land owners in the proposed Land Pooling Scheme by receiving irrevocable consent applications in Form -3 from the land owners; (iii) The Competent Authority may receive applications and shall issue an Official Receipt in Form No.4 (3) The notice shall contain the details of public purpose, area, extent, with survey numbers and reputed owners as available in Revenue Records along with a plan if any, and shall be published in the manner provid ed under section 136 of the APCRDA Act, 2014. (4) No notice under this rule shall be required if a notice under section 11(1) of The Right To Fair Compensation And Transparency In Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation And Resettlement Act, 2013 shall be deemed to be the area notified in Form11 under Land Pooling Scheme as per rule 5(2).

Vesting of land in Authority and issue of Land Pooling Ownership Certificate: (1) After notification of the final LPS, all the la nds shall vest absolutely in the Authority free from all encumbrances under section 5 7 and the District Collector, Guntur may summarily evict illegal occupants and h and over to the Competent Authority to enforce the scheme. (2) Within fifteen (15) days from the date of physic al marking of the reconstituted plots earmarked the allotment of reconstituted plot s shall be done to landowners by draw of lots, in an objective and transparent mann er with due publicity under video cover. (3) Within Fifteen (15) days of allotment, the Compe tent Authority of Mangalagiri Gold Cluster Land Pooling Scheme shall issue a Land Pooling Ownership Certificate [LPOC] in Form -12 , which shall be the final proof of the holder's title to that land and thereafter cause entry of such ownership details into the records of the registration department without any cost to the land owner. (4) The LPOC shall contain details of the land owner 's original land and reconstituted plot along with sketches. (5) The details of the LPOCs and parcels of land co ntributed by the land owners/assignees/encroachers etc., for establishment of Gems and Jewelry Park in Mangalagiri shall be made accessible to the public.

Powers of Competent Authority : (1) The Competent Authority or his officers shall b e competent to enter and conduct land survey, and establish the true area falling unde r the land pooling or to confirm true area of the claim of person/persons int erested and ascertain the original plot area or the apportionment of land, wherever required. 2) The Competent Authority or his officers shall hav e the powers to ascertain the ownership, extent and boundaries under Revenue Acts and other laws in general and specifically: (i) To summon and examine the witnesses or the records under the Andhra Pradesh Revenue Summons Act, 1969(Act 111 of 1869); (ii) To conduct enquires to apportion the respective claims among the multiple persons interested in a parcel of land; and (iii) To pass orders in Form -6 after establishing the ownership of the land 14. Miscellaneous: (1) The Authority's decision shall be final in all matters relating to Gems and Jewelry Park in Mangalagiri Gold Cluster. SCHEDULE 1 PROCESS OF THE SCHEME : (1) Notification of declaration of intention to pool lands. (2) Obtain irrevocable consents. (3) Invite general objections & suggestions on the intention, dispose objections & suggestions and notify final area under the scheme. (4) Conduct claim enquiry on consents and pass orde rs establishing ownership and execute Development Agreement 1cum1 irrevocable Ge neral Power of Attorney from the land owners besides taking physicalposses sion of land from the land owners. (5) Register the claims supported by ownership order s with Registration Department. (6) Refer unsettled disputes to District Collector, Guntur. (7) Prepare draft land pooling scheme, invite objec tions and notify final land pooling scheme. (8) Transfer of ownership of rights to the Authority for the purpose of implementing development scheme. (9) Allot reconstituted plots and issue LPOC as per Plot Allotment Policy.

items.text: GOVERNMENT OF ANDHRA PRADESH ABSTRACT MA&UD (CRDA) Department – AP Capital Region Development Authority (APCRDA) – Land Pooling Scheme (LPS) and Negotiated Settlement Policy (NSP) – Permission to utilise Aadhaar Authentication and e -KYC Services under Section 7 of the Aadhaar Act, 2016 – Issue of Gazette Notification – Orders – Issued. =============================================== MUNICIPAL ADMINISTRATION & URBAN DEVELOPMENT (CRDA) DEPARTMENT G.O.MS.No. 8 Dated: 23-01-2026 Read: From the Commissioner, APCRDA, Amarvati, Lr.No: MAU61 ADMN0IS (APWS)/6/2025-IS, Dated: 10-11-2025. -o0o- O R D E R: In the circumstances reported by the Commissioner, APCRDA, Amarvati , in the reference read above, wherein a proposal received requesting permission to utilise Aadhaar Authentication and e -KYC services under Section 7 of the Aadhaar Act, 2016 for the implementation of Land Pooling Scheme (LPS) and Negotiated Settlement Policy (NSP) applications of APCRDA. 2.
items.source: Andhra Pradesh G.O.MS-8 dated 23/01/2026: MA&UD (CRDA) Department – AP Capital Region Development Authority (APCRDA) – Land Pooling Scheme (LPS) and Negotiated Settlement Policy (NSP) – Permission to ut [MAUD department, 2026-01-23]
items.title: Andhra Pradesh G.O.MS-8 dated 23/01/2026: MA&UD (CRDA) Department – AP Capital Region Development Authority (APCRDA) – Land Pooling Scheme (LPS) and Negotiated Settlement Policy (NSP) – Permission to ut

items.text: 2. Government, after careful examination of the matter, hereby accord permission to APCRDA to utilise Aadhaar Authentication and e -KYC services under Section 7 of the Aadhaar Act, 2016 for implementation of Land Pooling Scheme (LPS) and Negotiated Settlement Policy (NSP). 3. A copy of this order is available on the Internet and can be accessed at:http://goir.ap.gov.in/. 4. Accordingly, the appended notification will be published in an extraordinary issue of the Andhra Pradesh Gazette, dated 23.01.2026. 5. The Commissioner, Printing, Stationery & Stores Purchase, Vijayawada, is requested to publish the said rules through notification and provide 300 copies of the same to the Government. (BY ORDER AND IN THE NAME OF THE GOVERNOR OF ANDHRA PRADESH) S SURESH KUMAR PRINCIPAL SECRETARY TO GOVERNMENT To The Commissioner, Printing, Stationery & Stores Purchase, Vijayawada. The Commissioner, Andhra Pradesh Capital Region Development Authority, Amaravati. Copy to : The ITE&C Department, AP Secretariat, Velgapudi. The PS to Hon’ble Minister for MA&UD. The PS to Principal Secretary to Government, MA&UD Dept., Sf/Sc //FORWARDED :: BY ORDER// SECTION OFFICER NOTIFICATION Whereas the use of Aadhaar number to establish identity enables individuals to receive subsidies, benefits and services in a convenient and seamless manner , obviates the need for multiplicity of documents to establish identity, simplifies processes and promotes transparency and efficiency: 2.

items.text: 2. And whereas Andhra Pradesh Capital Region Development Authority (APCRDA) (hereinafter referred to as the said agency) under the administrative purview of the Ministry of Municipal Administration and Urban Development Department (hereinafter referred to as the said Ministry or the said Department, as the case may be ) in the Government of Andhra Pradesh (hereinafter referred to as the said Government) is administ ering schemes Land Pooling Scheme (LPS) and Negotiated Settlement Policy (NSP) (hereinafter referred to as the said scheme): 3. And whereas returnable plots and annuity @ 50000/ - per Acre for Jareeb Lands and Rs. 30,000 per Acre for Dry lands, the same will be enhanced @ 10% on the base value every year under LPS and land to land along with monetary benefit includes 2 times of structure cost finalized by the R&B department and other allowances such as reconstruction cost, transportation for relocation, etc., under NSP scheme (hereinafter referred to as the said benefit) is given to the farmers / land owners who have given their land for the capital city (hereinafter referred to as the beneficiaries) under the said scheme and the instructions and guidelines issued in respect thereof: 4. And whereas expenditure for the said scheme is incurred from the Consolidated Fund of Government of Andhra Pradesh: 5.

items.text: 4. And whereas expenditure for the said scheme is incurred from the Consolidated Fund of Government of Andhra Pradesh: 5. And whereas the said APCRDA is desirous that the said Government , for the purpose of establishing identity of a beneficiary as a condition for the receipt of the said benefit, require that such beneficiary undergo authentication, or furnish proof of possession of Aadhaar number or in t he case of an individual to whom no Aadhaar number has been assigned, make an application for enrolment: 6. Now, therefore, in pursuance of the provisions of section 7 of the Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Service s) Act, 2016 (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Government of Andhra Pradesh hereby notifies the following, namely:— 1. (1) An individual desirous of availing of the said benefit under the said scheme shall be required to undergo authentication, or furnish proof of possession of Aadhaar number. (2) In case such an individual has not been assigned an Aadhaar number, he shall be required to make an application for enrolment: Provided that if that individual is a child, such application shall be made only with the consent of his parent or legal guardian.

items.text: GOVERNMENT OF ANDHRA PRADESH ABSTRACT MA & UD (CRDA) Dept. - APCRDA – Land Pooling Scheme – Amaravati Capital City – Commercial plots with road hits from W.SW & S.SW directions and plots with road hits from small road to large road widths / equal road widths – Treating as objectionable road-hit plots – Cancellation of such plots and allotment of alternate plots through lottery – Authorization to Commissioner, APCRDA – Orders – Issued. =============================================== MUNICIPAL ADMINISTRATION & URBAN DEVELOPMENT (CRDA) DEPARTMENT G.O.MS.No. 14 Dated: 29-01-2026 Read the following:- 1. From the Commissioner, CRDA, Vijayawada, Lr.No.MAU61- COOR0MEET (CM) /1/2026-OM, Dt. 07.01.2026. 2. Resolution No.623/2026, Dt.06.01.2026 of 57 th Meeting of the APCRDA. ORDER: In the reference 1 st read above, the Commissioner, APCRDA, Amaravati has stated that the 57th Meeting of the APCRDA Authority, held on 06.01.2026, has considered the issue of objectionable road hits in certain returnable plots allotted under the Land Pooling Scheme in the Capital City area and has passed Resolution No.623/2026, requesting Government to accord necessary approval for implementation of the decision taken therein. 2.
items.source: Andhra Pradesh G.O.MS-14 dated 29/01/2026: MA & UD (CRDA) Dept. - APCRDA – Land Pooling Scheme – Amaravati Capital City – Commercial plots with road hits from W.SW & S.SW directions and plots with road h [MAUD department, 2026-01-29]
items.title: Andhra Pradesh G.O.MS-14 dated 29/01/2026: MA & UD (CRDA) Dept. - APCRDA – Land Pooling Scheme – Amaravati Capital City – Commercial plots with road hits from W.SW & S.SW directions and plots with road h

items.text: 2. The APCRDA Authority, in its 57 th Meeting held on 06.01.2026, vide Resolution No.623/2026, has resolved to treat Category A, namely commercial plots with road hits from West–South West (W.SW) and South– South West (S.SW) directions, and Category B, namely plots with road hits from small road to large road widths and equal road widths, where such road hits fall under objectionable category, as objectionable road-hit plots. The Authority has further resolved that such plots shall be cancelled and allotted alternate plots through a lottery system, based on representations received from the allottees, subject to the condition that the plots have not been mutated to third party. The successful and effective implementation of any initiative or programme in government is largely the result of the involvement and efforts put in by its functionaries at all levels. Obviously, the most fruitful way in which to bring this about is to make individual functionaries aware of their role functions and responsibilities. To achieve this, the Human Resource Development Institute of AP, as the apex training institution of the State Government responsible for the overall implementation and co ordination of the state training initiative, has proposed to bring out departmentwise Manuals in two parts, namely శ Departmental Manual బే Functionary Manual The Departmental Manual! would indicate the role, responsibilities and functions of the department. The Functionary Manual will detail, as the nomenclature indicates, the functions and responsibilities of the functionaries within the department, at all levels. While doing so, the evolving role of governmental functionaries in being effective managers of change in a welfare state has been delineated. The Departmental Manual also details the department's organisational chart, the rules, regulations,legislations and enactments which govern its functioning and direct its activities and the various interdepartmental interactions it has to perform.

items.text: The Departmental Manual also details the department's organisational chart, the rules, regulations,legislations and enactments which govern its functioning and direct its activities and the various interdepartmental interactions it has to perform. The Manual also facilitates a definition of the department's role in serving the general public as customer while drawing up a vision for its future development in the coming decades. The present Volumes are in 2 parts developed by the Horticulture Department. As is evident, these publications are the outcome of thorough study and analysis of the department's role, functions and procedures. They are intended to serve as useful aid to every employee of he department in the effective discharge of his functions. It may be noted, however, that these Manuals do not replace the Codes Manuals and Orders on the subject but are, at best, meant to guide and assist the functionaries in the effective discharge of their duties. Jurisdiction:- The Director of Horticulture / Commissioner of Horticulture is the Head of the Department and is competent to take independent decisions in all matters of expenditure against the sanction of programmes. GARDENS SECTION HISTORY AND FORMATION OF THE DEPARTMENT (PUBLIC GARDENS) The public gardens was established in 54 acres of land which belonged to Sri.Balakrishnan in the year 1868 A.D. consisting of some babul ( Acacia Aratica) and other species of trees. It was Originally known as (Bagh-E-Am) Subsequently an engineer of his exceilency of Nizam's Government made improvements and completed in 1872 under the supervision of Sir Wlikison,an engineer. A zoo was added with many kinds of birds, forest and wild animals in the year 1872. The (Bagh-E- Am) is only the place where recreation for the public was available and the zoo was also visited by the various people of different walks of life. Certain improvements were made by Sir Mirza Islam, when he was the president of the council of Ministers Hyderabad. The Gardens were maintained by the Superintendent , Government Gardens attached to the PWD department. The post if the superintendent was redesignated as director of Government Gardens in G.O.Ms.No. 2353 PWD dt, 24-9- 65. The Director of Government Gardens was merged with the Agricul- ture Department dated 12-2-1976.

Dt. 12-3-91. The post has been sanctioned under CERP during 1990-91 through Government Order. During the May 1990 a severe cyclonic storm has divested coconut gar- dens besides other horticultural crops in the coastal districts of Andhra Pradesh. Coconut is mostly concentrated in the coastal districts of Khammam and Chittoor. Several areas in the districts of Krishna, Khammam, West and East Godavari districts were forced for replanting of coconut on account of cyclonic damage. Further, the normal practice in these areas is to plant East Coast tall variety without following the norms recommended for selection of seed nuts and seedlings. Coconut hybridization was being practiced at harvest minimal in East Godavari district. Therefore it is thought that this is opportune time to upgrade the quality of planting time to fulfill the above need and objective the Gov- ernment were pleased to sanction the coconut seed garden in Aswaraopet Khammam district. The seed garden is headed by a Dy. Director of Horticulture.
